acceptance_criteria.description: Concurrent first-Admin invocations serialize on the Account table and create exactly one active ADMIN with one audit entry.
evidence: tests/integration/identity/admin-bootstrap.test.ts concurrently invokes three service calls and observes one created result, two already_provisioned results, one ADMIN and one account.admin_provisioned audit entry.

tests/unit/identity/bootstrap.test.ts asserts lockAccountTableForFirstAdmin precedes Admin count and Account insert precedes AuditEntry; the iteration diff shows the repository method issuing exact SQL LOCK TABLE app.account IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE.

acceptance_criteria.description: Admin existence alone provides idempotency, while normalized-email conflict never promotes a USER.
evidence: Unit and PostgreSQL tests return already_provisioned without Account or AuditEntry writes after an Admin exists.
The PostgreSQL conflict case preserves the existing role USER, creates zero Admins and writes no provisioning audit entry.

acceptance_criteria.description: Account and AuditEntry creation are atomic and dependency failure maps safely to unavailable.
evidence: The PostgreSQL audit-failure case observes ServiceUnavailableError and zero Admin/AuditEntry rows after rollback.
The route unit suite maps ServiceUnavailableError to the safe 503 service_unavailable envelope without raw dependency details.

acceptance_criteria.description: The approved HTTP mapping and precedence are enforced solely by availability plus the deployment secret, with no browser authority or sensitive output.
evidence: tests/unit/auth/bootstrap-route.test.ts covers missing/wrong secret 403 with no Identity call, disabled config 503 before a deliberately wrong secret, conflict 409, distinct created/already 200 bodies, dependency 503, new request ID, and ignored cookies/session/CSRF/Origin.
Response/log assertions exclude the supplied secret, configured email and configured password.

acceptance_criteria.description: Readiness remains unavailable without an Admin and uses typed control flow, while it becomes ready after an Admin exists.
evidence: Focused unit tests cover valid and absent bootstrap configuration with no Admin, timeout and query failure classification.
The PostgreSQL health suite returns the identical unavailable public body with no Admin and returns ready only after inserting an Admin.

acceptance_criteria.description: The legacy singleton table, methods, migration, privileges and schema expectations are fully removed.
evidence: Read-only scan reports MIGRATION_ABSENT and no app.admin_bootstrap, lockBootstrap or completeBootstrap reference in src/tests.
Fresh-schema object, constraint and privilege tests passed as part of the focused and full PostgreSQL suites.

acceptance_criteria.description: Build/module initialization and ordinary startup do not invoke first-Admin bootstrap.
evidence: Route-module initialization unit test dynamically imports a fresh route/composition mock and observes zero bootstrap calls.
npm run build -- --webpack completed all production build phases without bootstrap invocation and emitted the bootstrap endpoint as a dynamic route.
